target_claim.subject: al-Qurtubi's Sūrah 108:1 cross-reference to al-Tadhkira and the four-caliphs cluster
target_claim.review_question: Does a source-specific witness for al-Tadhkira support treating this as al-Qurtubi's own cross-reference/discussion, separate from the quoted Sahih Muslim/Anas report, and what locator can be stated without conflating editions?
target_claim.bounded_finding: A digital transcription of al-Tadhkira contains its own chapter on the Prophet's cistern and, within that chapter, a four-corners/four-caliphs passage. The same text attributes a report through the Ghaylaniyyat and quotes a Hamid-from-Anas route; this checkpoint records the text's attribution only and makes no authenticity, route-independence, or historical-transmission judgment. A separate catalog contents page for the al-Sadiq edition locates the cistern chapter at vol. 2, p. 702; it does not establish that the unpaginated digital transcription is that edition or map the live source ID 671 to it.
target_claim.voice_boundary: The Sūrah 108:1 wording is al-Qurtubi's authorial cross-reference/additional discussion, not part of the adjacent Muslim/Anas quotation and not Ata's attributed opinion.
